trust_decision.summary: n8n's expression engine substitutes workflow/item data into the 'Database Path' (db_path) node parameter, so data-controlled text becomes the filesystem path handed to better-sqlite3's open(); the published decision is to forbid data expressions on that property by setting noDataExpression: true on the v1 field descriptor.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the db_path parameter, and this is the only property with name 'db_path' in the tree; its descriptor (lines 111-118) lacks the noDataExpression flag that neighbouring query_type (line 124) already has.

fix_sites.entry_point: SQLite node version 1 execution handler (SqliteV1.execute, nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:188), reached by running any workflow step that uses sqliteNode version 1
fix_sites.module_kind: n8n node type description (INodeTypeDescription property metadata) consumed by the node handler

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: nodes/SqliteNode/v2/transport/index.ts:15-35 — the v2 node opens the same SQLite file via new Database(dbPath), but takes the path from a credential field (credentials/SqliteCredentials.credentials.ts:11-19) that also has no noDataExpression; the published fix touched only the v1 node property

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The v2 path is an admin-set credential ('Database File Path', credentials only) rather than a node parameter, and n8n credentials cannot reference item data, so a solver can argue the advisory — which names the db_path node parameter and was committed as 'fix(v1)' — does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: db_path must keep accepting arbitrary literal paths: relative names such as 'test.sqlite', absolute paths, and paths whose parent directory does not exist yet (the handler creates the directory, nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:208-222). A path.resolve/allowlist-root or 'reject traversal/absolute paths' fix breaks documented and tested usage; the same over-broad instinct would also break the additionalOptions.use_custom_bindings path, which is legitimately a filesystem path to a better-sqlite3 binding file.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: nodes/SqliteNode/v1/__tests__/SqliteV1.node.test.ts:34 (relative db_path) and :216 (use_custom_bindings path passed through untouched)

O6_input_shapes: plain literal string path (must stay allowed)
full expression path such as ={{ $json.path }} (result of the fix: expression evaluation disabled)
expression referencing item fields ($json / $item()), evaluated once per input item at nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:193 (disabled)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: v2 node execution resolves the SQLite file path from the sqliteCredentials 'databasePath' field and opens it (per item run) without any expression guard on that credential field
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a credential, not the db_path node parameter; credentials are administrator-set and are not evaluated against item data, so the advisory's parameter-level protection is argued not to apply.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (nodes/SqliteNode/v2) plus credentials/ — 2 directories and 2 files away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: credential verification (testedBy sqliteConnectionTest) opens the same database file from the credential before any node runs
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is credential validation, not node execution, and it only proves the file is openable, so a solver can call it a neighbouring feature rather than a data path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: nodes/SqliteNode/v2/methods, separate file from the transport and the router

O8_uncovered_routes.route: parameter-dropdown helpers getColumns / getColumnsMultiOptions / searchTables silently open the database from the credential while the user edits the node
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: UI loadOptions/listSearch methods are editor-time convenience calls, not the execute path the advisory describes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: nodes/SqliteNode/v2/methods/loadOptions.ts and listSearch.ts:7 — two more files in a sibling directory

O8_uncovered_routes.route: v1 additionalOptions.use_custom_bindings is a user-controlled filesystem path checked with fs.existsSync and passed to better-sqlite3 as nativeBinding
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It selects which better-sqlite3 binary to load rather than the database file, so it looks like a build/portability option and not the db_path sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different property (collection-nested), 60 lines from the fixed descriptor

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the v1 'Query' field accepts data expressions while v2's equivalent already sets noDataExpression (nodes/SqliteNode/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts:26)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding the same guard to db_path would plausibly add it to the sibling Query field in the same properties array, following the v2 precedent.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second filesystem-path string (use_custom_bindings) nested in the additionalOptions collection, with a real absolute-path default
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The node genuinely needs a user-supplied binding path for non-docker installs, so the field cannot be removed; it can only be guarded the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second credential property (e.g. an attaches/extra database file path) that reaches the same createConnection/new Database sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Adding 'Attach Database File' as a credential option is a natural feature for a SQLite node and would copy the existing property shape without the flag.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new operation taking a file path (e.g. ATTACH DATABASE / backup-to-file) defined as a plain string parameter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The v2 resource already grows one operation file per action, and every existing operation's non-path parameters are plain strings; a path parameter would follow that pattern.

O9_family: path traversal / expression injection into a filesystem path (CWE-22)

O10_build.toolchain: npm scripts: build = rimraf + tsc (typescript ^5.8.2) + gulp build:icons; test = jest 29 with ts-jest preset (jest.config.js); eslint 8; better-sqlite3 ^12.6.2 with a vendored prebuilt binding at native/node-v127-linux-musl-x64/better_sqlite3.node
O10_build.project_tests: jest suites: nodes/SqliteNode/v1/__tests__/SqliteV1.node.test.ts (mocks better-sqlite3 and fs, exercises relative db_path and use_custom_bindings), nodes/SqliteNode/v2/actions/database/__tests__/operations.test.ts, nodes/SqliteNode/v2/helpers/__tests__/utils.test.ts; none assert node-description metadata such as noDataExpression

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add runtime path validation in execute() (path.resolve + allowed-root check, reject '..' or absolute paths) before new Database(dbPath), instead of setting noDataExpression on the property descriptor — behaviour looks fixed but the metadata assertion the published fix encodes still fails, and the validation breaks relative/literal paths.

out_of_scope_notes: nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:65-68: additionalOptions.use_custom_bindings is an arbitrary user-supplied filesystem path handed to better-sqlite3 as nativeBinding, i.e. loading an arbitrary native shared object (CWE-426/CWE-94 family) — noted, not pursued.
unverified: Whether n8n evaluates expressions inside credential fields was not checked: n8n-workflow is a peerDependency and node_modules is absent at the pinned commit, so the v2 credential route (O2/O8) may not carry the same taint as a node parameter. This is the single biggest uncertainty behind pattern_fit=B.
Repo size in MB not measured (no shell in this session); the tree is ~35 source files with the largest at ~270 lines, so tiny_repo is asserted from the file listing rather than a size measurement.
O4 counts are hops, not measured path lengths: 3 files / 3 directories separate nodes/SqliteNode/v1 from credentials/ and nodes/SqliteNode/v2.
Downloaded dependencies are required before build/test (no node_modules in the pinned tree), so the first build needs a registry or cache even though the built code and tests run offline.
No release or later commit was in scope for O8 'present_in_latest', so every route is marked unknown.

The published fix has no behavioural code and no tests; a hidden test can only assert the property metadata (possibly by instantiating SqliteV1 and reading .description.properties), which no existing test does — fairness of grading an equivalent runtime validation is unresolved.
